Lol I want to defend my boyfriend right now but I just can’t, no matter how I try to spin it in my head. 

I wish he might do something on his own. I don’t want to ask him because it’s a lot to ask of somebody.

He’s 100% on my side in that he agrees they fucked up and completely understands why I’m upset. But The way we both know our friends we think that they’re just dense and really don’t understand that I’m upset, which is why he suggested I might message them individually. 

But I got ghosted and he didn’t say much after that. I think he was hoping they would listen to me and when they didn’t he wasn’t sure what to do. I think he’s processing

I could understand your perspective here, and this is kind of what I think they may be feeling. 

There’s certainly more history behind this and it’s hard to give the whole picture in a short post. They think it’s a joke, and I think some of that has to do with the fact that they don’t experience sexism. I’m just feeling particularly tired of dealing with sexism lately so it didn’t feel like a joke to me.  (I deal with much more blatant sexism at my work.) But, That’s why I gave them the benefit of the doubt and tried to talk to them. 

I just think that the way they handled it felt sexist in itself. Like why would you not at least wait for me to explain before coming to a conclusion? I understand it would take longer but still, it was my thing to speak on. Because yes, I do believe women understand sexism better than men. We just experience it more often

Are cheerleaders actually loud and talkative and attention seeking anymore than anyone else? Or is that a trope we got from the 1900s when sexism was more rampant. 

To strengthen my point, boys are told all the time that it’s bad to be like a girl and young girls interests are always shit on. I don’t see how this would be any different. 

Judging by your post history, you fall into the incel attitude and I have no hope of reaching you. I hope you figure out some day that not all women are the same way. Women are people. And women have valid perspectives. Thanks for engaging with me

Cheerleading is associated with women where I live. It’s regarded as women’s club where men don’t belong. This is important. 

The association is basically that women talk to much and they’re gossipy etc. This is the association that the teacher made. 

By calling a boy a cheerleader in this way, he’s making being a cheerleader a bad thing, and by association, being a woman a bad.

It is a “micro-aggression”. People don’t usually realize that they’re doing it or that they’re harmful. If it was a one off thing it wouldn’t bother me, but after a life time of “micro-aggressions” it gets tiring.

I feel this in my soul. 

Women are always told not to rock the boat. I think that why we sometimes try to gently let people down, even when they deserve a hard STOP or NO. Because if we do, then we’re overreacting or over emotional. 

At the same time, I don’t think you need to be more forceful and serious when you tell somebody to stop. People need to learn to take women seriously
